subject: Post-demo follow-up: data handling, residency, and DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medisynchealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: data handling, residency, and DPA clarifications

Hi Olivia —

Great to meet today — thanks for carving out time for the demo. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can get legal and procurement aligned before the next call: 

- Demo highlights: Redwood hosted inference (EU + US regions), dedicated pools for predictable throughput, built-in KV/prefix caching to reduce token costs.
- Open questions from your side we promised to follow up on: PII/PHI scope, data residency options for EU-only, logging/retention windows, and breach/notice timelines in the DPA addendum.

Can you confirm the types of data you expect to send to Redwood during inference (examples: full patient record, hashed identifiers only, device telemetry)? That will help our legal/product teams map controls. Also, do you require contract language that designates MediSync as the controller and Redwood as the processor (we can include the standard processor clauses and an addendum to enumerate subprocessors)?

I attached a short DPA summary and a current subprocessors export to speed review. Proposed next steps:
1) If you can share the canonical list of data fields (PII/PHI examples) we’ll route to Product for precise retention/logging guidance.
2) If legal wants a redline call, happy to schedule (Ben can join).
3) We’ll confirm residency options and propose explicit wording for breach notification windows (we typically commit to "as soon as reasonably possible" but can discuss a firm window for high-severity incidents).

Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf (pdf, 82KB), redwood-subprocessors-20270403.csv (csv, 4KB)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0172
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medisynchealth.com>

Thanks Rachel — great demo. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Data types: We will be sending a mix. The core inference payload will include patient identifiers (MRN, hashed SSN), free-text clinical notes (may contain PHI), and device telemetry (non-identifying). We can produce a field-level sample extract for Product.
- Residency: For regulatory reasons we need EU residency for EU patient data. Does Redwood provide EU-only processing for hosted customers, or would we need a Private deployment?
- Subprocessors: Please provide an export with names and locations (we'll need to run vendor checks).
- Breach timelines: Our legal expects an explicit breach notification window in the DPA. Would Redwood commit to notification within 72 hours of discovery for incidents affecting PHI?

I’ve attached our security questionnaire and can loop in our procurement lead if helpful. Also, please confirm retention windows for raw request logs and KV cache (we need to know how long identifiers could be reconstructed).

Attachment: SecurityQuestionnaire_MediSync.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

Olivia Park
Head of Product Ops | MediSync Health

Subject: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up: data handling, residency, and DPA clarifications

Forwarding Olivia's note — see inline suggestions below. I flagged Product and Legal items.

--- Ben's notes (inline):
- Data types: ask for sample payload (field-level) — Product needs that to advise on tokenization and redaction options.
- Residency: Hosted EU regions are available for customers on our Hosted plan, but guaranteed EU-only residency for contractual purposes is provided via our Private (VPC) option. Product: confirm whether we can offer "EU processing only" for a hosted Enterprise instance with contractual controls.
- Subprocessors: attach current export (redwood-subprocessors-20270403.csv). Legal: please confirm whether we can commit to listing subprocessors and notify customers 30 days before adding high-risk subprocessors (standard approach).
- Breach timelines: Legal to weigh in, but practice is to notify as soon as reasonably possible; committing to a fixed 72-hour SLA is a negotiation.

Attachment: DPA_markedup.docx (docx, 34KB)

—Ben

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@medisynchealth.com>, legal@medisynchealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: data handling, residency, and DPA clarifications

Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Below are consolidated answers from Product + Legal to help you and procurement review quickly. If helpful we can schedule a short redline call with our legal counsel.

1) Controller / Processor
- Canonical position: MediSync (you) are the Controller; Redwood is the Processor when you send inference payloads to our hosted endpoints. We will accept customer-directed processing instructions and can include the standard processor commitments in the DPA addendum.

2) Subprocessors
- See attached current export (redwood-subprocessors-20270403.csv) with vendor name and country. We commit to providing 30-days notice for new high-risk subprocessors and publish a live subprocessors page.

3) Data residency
- Hosted: we operate in US and EU regions; hosted EU nodes are physically located in EU data centers but some admin/control-plane metadata may cross borders. For strict contractual EU-only residency (no cross-border processing of EU personal data), the Private deployment (VPC) is the recommended route. We can propose language to make residency explicit depending on the deployment option you choose.

4) Retention and logging
- Default inference request logs: 90 days.
- KV cache: ephemeral by default (48 hours) unless a customer opts into extended cache retention; we can quote extended retention separately and include controls for key rotation.
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics: retained for 1 year for observability.

5) Breach notification
- Legal note: Redwood will notify customers as soon as reasonably possible after confirming the scope and impact; for incidents affecting PHI we can agree to an objective escalation path and use "initial notification within 48-72 hours" for high-severity incidents while we work toward precise SLA language in the DPA redline. Committing to a strict 72-hour legal SLA is a negotiation point for our contracts team.

Next steps:
- Rachel: can you share a sample field-level payload by Monday (will route to Product for tokenization/redaction guidance)?
- Olivia/legal: if you can propose 2 times for a redline call this week, we'll bring counsel and a product engineer.
- We'll upload a marked-up DPA and SOC2 snapshot for your review.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf, SOC2-snapshot.pdf, redwood-subprocessors-20270403.csv

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks,
Olivia
